_readme: Improvements to the site and the method, each tied to the evidence that motivated it and to a decision a reviewer can actually make. 'effort' is a rough size, not a schedule. 'needs' says what must exist before it can be done. Nothing here is implemented in this session unless it is the page you are reading.
review_process: A reviewer reads the ranking, picks a path per suggestion, and records the pick. An unrecorded pick is a suggestion, not a decision. Sorted by value per unit of effort, ties broken by what unblocks the most readiness rows.

rows.title: Run the collector, then let the failing gate pass on its own
rows.evidence: The corpus holds 137 completed games; the official standings imply 149. tools/verify_official.py check E fails because of it, and three committed standings copies are 3-4 days stale (6 of 32 clubs still match).
rows.recommended_path: Trigger the collect-data workflow, re-derive, and re-publish. Do not edit the check.
rows.alternative: Freeze corpus v2 by hand — slower, and it leaves the same lag in a week.
rows.unblocks: 4 readiness rows, 1 failing CI job, 3 stale files
rows.risk: A collector run changes numbers several pages quote; the pages regenerate from data, so this is a rebuild, not a rewrite.
rows.needs: Nothing. The workflow exists and is scheduled daily at 11:17 UTC.

rows.title: Take the price-policy decision so pricing can start
rows.evidence: price_policy.state is 'open decision'; there is one value per market per game and no fetch clock, so opening/closing numbers and a de-vigged consensus cannot be built.
rows.recommended_path: Write a one-page policy: the source, the read times (say T-24h and T-1h), and what happens when a price is missing. Sign and date it in data/prereg/ before any backtest that uses a price is published.
rows.alternative: Score on observed closing prices only and label every ROI as closing-line ROI — honest, but it cannot measure line movement.
rows.unblocks: P-01, P-06, P-07 and every priced backtest
rows.risk: Choosing a source that later disappears invalidates history; prefer one with a documented retention policy.

rows.title: Rank only prospective, settled rows; move the 12 backtest rows to an archive page
rows.evidence: 31 strategies are registered but the s9cb leaderboard still ranks 12 backtest rows by ROI. The brief forbids backtest numbers on the leaderboard; the page labels them but still ranks them.
rows.recommended_path: Split the page: a ranked prospective board (currently 0 settled bets) and a clearly separated archive of backtest rows with their sample and selection caveat.
rows.alternative: Keep one page and remove the rank column from backtest rows — cheaper, but readers still sort by ROI.
rows.unblocks: S-04, and the credibility of every later promotion
rows.risk: The board becomes visibly empty, which is the honest state.

rows.title: Add the moneyline to the originated board
rows.evidence: 13 side lines and 13 totals exist; no moneyline price is produced, though the win probability that would generate one is already stored (my_win_prob_home).
rows.recommended_path: Derive a two-way moneyline from the stored win probability, publish it beside side and total, and leave the market column blank until a price source exists.
rows.alternative: Publish only the probability — less useful to a reader comparing to a market.
rows.risk: A derived moneyline inherits every error in the probability; label it as derived.

rows.title: Render depth slots as groups, with blanks shown
rows.evidence: The club charts put up to four names in one cell (Lions TE, Lions CB), print a jersey number inside the name (Packers), and leave a cell empty (Ravens kicker, Packers punt returner). The register models one name per slot.
rows.recommended_path: Store a list of names per slot plus the raw cell text, render every name, and print an explicit 'club lists no player' for an empty cell.
rows.alternative: Keep one name per slot and label rank 1 'listed first', never 'the starter'.
rows.risk: Touches a register another generator owns; log the request rather than editing it.
rows.needs: A schema change in the ownership of data/depth/official_register.json.

rows.title: Label every context column official or third-party, on the page
rows.evidence: Rest days, roof, surface and referee columns come from a third-party parse. The site cites nfl.com beside rows whose numbers did not come from nfl.com.
rows.recommended_path: Add an 'origin' column to every context table: 'nfl.com page' or 'nflverse parse'. Where a row mixes both, split it.
rows.alternative: Cite the third-party licence in the footer only — cheaper, and it is what the site does today.
rows.risk: Several rows become partly blank, which is the point.

rows.title: Capture the report on Wed, Thu and Fri, and publish the delta between reads
rows.evidence: One parsed report exists. The brief asks for a timestamped series and a published delta; a level cannot show a Questionable -> Out move.
rows.recommended_path: Keep the 6-hourly job, add a report-day filter so the captures land on Wed/Thu/Fri, and publish a delta table keyed by player with the clock time of each read.
rows.alternative: Capture hourly — more data, no more information than the league publishes.
rows.risk: A capture taken after a game has started is a leak; record kickoff and refuse to publish a late read as pre-game.

rows.title: Publish the club-code crosswalk used by every join
rows.evidence: One club is AZ on two official pages and ARI in a committed capture; the Rams are LA on nfl.com and LAR on their own site. Joins silently depend on a mapping nobody publishes.
rows.recommended_path: A small table: printed code, normalised code, the page that prints it. Render the printed value beside the normalised one wherever a join matters.

rows.title: Publish the corpus lag as a number on the dashboard, not only in a failing check
rows.evidence: A reader cannot tell from the dashboard that the ratings are 12 games behind the official season.
rows.recommended_path: One row: completed games in the corpus, games implied by the official standings, and the difference, with the date each was read.
rows.alternative: Leave it to CI — but CI is not on the page a reader opens.

rows.title: Read the remaining 28 club charts once, and record HTML vs image
rows.evidence: 3 of 32 clubs transcribed; one club publishes its chart as an image and cannot be read without a structured source.
rows.recommended_path: One pass per club: URL, whether the table is machine-readable, and a hash of the page. Publish the coverage count either way.
rows.alternative: Do nothing and keep the 3-club sample with an explicit coverage caveat, as this page does.
rows.risk: 28 pages is enough for a parser to break silently on one; the hash and the row count are the alarm.

rows.title: Run the injury/personnel ablation as a pre-registered test, not a feature
rows.evidence: The model applies a fixed penalty instead of testing whether personnel features help. With one availability capture the test would measure leakage, not skill.
rows.recommended_path: Register the ablation now (two identical fits, with and without availability, paired difference on a chronological holdout) and run it when the snapshot series has at least two weeks that predate kickoffs.
rows.alternative: Skip it and state that personnel is not modelled — defensible, and cheaper.
rows.risk: A leaked run would produce a flattering number; the gate must refuse to score a fixture without a pre-kickoff read.

rows.title: Make the readiness table the site's front page, with the blocker and the number
rows.evidence: Every prior generation put a summary on the landing page and the blockers on a sub-page. A reader then has to hunt for what stops the project.
rows.recommended_path: Front page = one row per requirement, the blocking gate, the number now, the number that clears it. Summary text underneath, not above.
rows.alternative: Keep a narrative summary and link the table — pleasant, but it hides the gates.
rows.risk: The front page looks unfinished, because most rows are not met. That is the true state.
